answer: Each agent identity must pass latency triangulation: independent beacons send timed probes, and the agent replies from its claimed location. Real machines produce distinct latency signatures, while Sybil copies on one server answer with near-identical delays, as if written by the same quill. Suspect clusters merge into one identity, so a cedar-strong reputation is shared, not multiplied. To evade this, an attacker must rent dispersed machines in many cities, paying real hosting per identity. The ember of free duplication dies: a thousand fake agents cost roughly a thousand times more than one.
